_real_world.variant_scope: AN/APG-79 as fitted to F/A-18E/F Block II/III Super Hornet and EA-18G Growler
public_equipment: AN/APG-79 AESA, X-band, 150 km range class (Raytheon/missiledefenseadvocacy public spec)

_provenance.modeling_note: Primary fire-control radar for CVW-8's F/A-18E/F and EA-18G. The CSG order-of-battle page confirms the AESA designation only via Tier C but gives no detection range; max_range is web-sourced. Scan/track/noise parameters (fov_deg, scan_period, detection_prob, bearing/range_noise_std, track_memory_s, range_power, aspect_influence, doppler_notch_width) have no public figures and are proxy values patterned on the repo AN/APG-68(V)9 record (aircraft/modules/sensors/an_apg_68.json), adjusted modestly upward for detection_prob and downward for noise terms to reflect the AESA's solid-state, faster-scan advantage over the APG-68's mechanically-scanned array, per the public qualitative claims (RTX, NAVAIR) of improved tracking/reliability.

sensor.max_range.note: 150 km detection/track range, Wikipedia and Missile Defense Advocacy Alliance both cite 150 km; no Tier A/B figure found in 2 searches

sensor.fov_deg.note: proxy from repo AN/APG-68(V)9 (aircraft/modules/sensors/an_apg_68.json); AESA arrays typically have a wider mechanical+electronic FOV but no public figure found

sensor.scan_period.note: engineering_estimate halved vs repo APG-68's 2.0 s to reflect AESA electronic (non-mechanical) beam-steering speed advantage claimed qualitatively by RTX/NAVAIR sources

sensor.detection_prob.note: engineering_estimate slightly above repo APG-68's 0.9, reflecting AESA reliability/performance improvement claims (RTX, NAVAIR); no quantified public figure

sensor.bearing_noise_std.note: engineering_estimate slightly below repo APG-68's 0.5, same AESA-precision reasoning

sensor.range_noise_std.note: engineering_estimate below repo APG-68's 20.0, same AESA-precision reasoning

sensor.track_memory_s.note: proxy close to repo APG-68's 5.0 s; no public figure

sensor.range_power.note: proxy copied unchanged from repo APG-68 (radar-equation exponent, not platform-specific)
